title: PowerPoint on the web: attach and reference an image when creating a presentation with Copilot Agent Mode
summary: The roadmap facts, image-attachment workflow, licence assignment path and PowerShell call are supported. Minor corrections should preserve the privacy documentation's current-version qualification, acknowledge Microsoft's separate guidance on web connected-experience controls, and reconcile the browser-policy checklist with the controls table.

claims.where: summary; Governance controls; Open questions; defaultState
claims.claim: No feature-specific administrator setting for attaching an image is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint Copilot Agent Mode attach reference image administrator disable policy Graph license image referencing; PowerPoint image attachment admin Copilot Graph. Read release-notes, copilot-overview and returned brand-image/agent-control guidance; no image-attachment switch found.

claims.claim: No source found states that this update changes existing behaviour for users who do not attach an image.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint Copilot Agent Mode attach reference image administrator disable policy Graph license image referencing; PowerPoint Copilot attach reference image Basic Premium license pricing meter Agent Mode. Read release-notes image entry and copilot-overview; no such change stated.

claims.claim: The release note describes no new permission, identity or sign-in step for attaching an image.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint Copilot Agent Mode attach reference image administrator disable policy Graph license image referencing. Read the complete release-notes image entry: its steps open a presentation, attach an image in the Copilot pane and review slides; no new identity or permission step.

claims.claim: No documentation found explains an additional Agent Mode mechanism for this attached-image feature beyond the release-note workflow.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint Agent Mode image licensing controls; PowerPoint Copilot Agent Mode attach reference image administrator disable policy Graph license image referencing. Read release-notes and returned Word/Excel/PowerPoint Agents guidance, which concerns separate agents in the Copilot app.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Billing > Licenses > product > Assign licenses reaches licence assignment.
claims.quote: In the admin center, go to the Billing > Licenses page. Select a product. On the product details page, select Assign licenses.

claims.claim: Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @() assigns a licence using Microsoft Graph PowerShell.
claims.quote:
To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell.
Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.claim: Licence assignment requires at least License Administrator or User Administrator.
claims.quote: You must be at least a License or User Administrator to assign licenses.

claims.claim: The user-scoped licence assignment control gives Copilot-in-PowerPoint entitlement, not a separate image-attachment switch.
claims.quote: You have the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license with access to the full experience of Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote.

claims.claim: Third-party cookies must be enabled for Copilot to work in PowerPoint for the web.
claims.quote: For Copilot to work in Word for the web, Excel for the web, and PowerPoint for the web, third-party cookies must be enabled.

claims.claim: The roadmap record and image-referencing release-note entry state no administrator role for using the feature.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint Copilot Agent Mode attach reference image administrator disable policy Graph license image referencing. Read the roadmap record and complete release-notes image entry; neither names an administrator role for the user workflow.

claims.claim: Turning off connected experiences that analyze content makes Copilot unavailable in PowerPoint and the other named apps on the documented devices.
claims.quote: If you turn off connected experiences that analyze your content on devices in your organization, Microsoft Copilot features won't be available to your users in the following apps: Excel; OneNote; Outlook; PowerPoint; Word.

claims.claim: The privacy page names Windows, Mac, iOS and Android for this connected-experience control.
claims.quote: This applies to when you're running the most current version of these apps on Windows, Mac, iOS, or Android devices.
claims.fix: Replace 'and it names Windows, Mac, iOS and Android devices' with 'and says this applies when running the most current version of these apps on Windows, Mac, iOS or Android devices'.

claims.where: Governance controls; Open questions: connected experiences
claims.claim: The cited privacy page's analyze-content sentence does not name the web.
claims.quote: This applies to when you're running the most current version of these apps on Windows, Mac, iOS, or Android devices.
claims.fix: Keep the accurate observation about the cited sentence, but replace the final Open questions bullet with: 'Microsoft's sensitive and regulated customer guidance says Copilot requires the Analyze Content connected experience category and that web experiences are controlled exclusively by Cloud Policy.' Cite and add to sources https://learn.microsoft.com/compliance/anz/blueprint-copilot-reqconfig#connected-experiences. That page states: 'The web experiences and modern apps are controlled exclusively by the Cloud Policy.'

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The checklist tells administrators to check browser policy, but the controls table has no corresponding browser-policy row.
claims.quote: Check that browser policy allows third-party cookies for PowerPoint for the web. The table's sole row governs which users hold the Microsoft 365 Copilot licence.
claims.fix: Replace the Before rollout browser-policy bullet with 'Confirm that Copilot works in PowerPoint for the web before communicating the feature.' Retain the documented third-party-cookie prerequisite in Scope; do not add an unverified control row.
